# Decision-Point Surface Audit

<!-- last_updated: 2026-09-03 -->

**Date**: 2026-07-26
**Task**: `scutemob-148`
**Bug class**: A point where the Comprehensive Rules give a *player* a choice, but the engine
makes that choice itself — deterministically, legally, and invisibly — because no `Command`
carries the player's answer.
**Scope**: read-only audit of the whole decision surface. No engine, simulator, card-def or
test change. The only files this task writes are this document and its index line in
[README.md](README.md).
**Motivation**: the 2026-07-26 finding that triggered-ability targets are auto-selected
engine-side (`abilities.rs:7174-7500`, proposed seed OOS-M11-4; renumbered from OOS-M11-3 at collection — scutemob-147 independently claimed OOS-M11-3 for fuzzer long-game nondeterminism), plus M11-local building a
human-input game loop whose decision surface must be known to be complete before the loop is
designed around it.

> **Severity-tally disambiguation** — same convention as
> [layer-bypass-audit.md](layer-bypass-audit.md). The class-B and class-D findings catalogued
> here are this audit's own class. They are **not** the "0 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 6 LOW" engine
> tally in `CLAUDE.md` → Current State, which counts the milestone-review issue index. Both
> are correct at once. Nothing here is scheduled yet; §8 proposes a queue, it does not create
> one.

---

## 1. The invariant

Per [methodology.md](methodology.md) Step 1, the property this audit tests is stated
declaratively:

> **DP-INV**: For every decision the CR assigns to a player, the engine either (a) obtains
> that player's answer through a `Command`, or (b) refuses to admit into a game any card
> that would reach the decision.

Branch (b) already exists and is machine-enforced. Architecture Invariant 9 / SR-2 make
`validate_deck` reject any card whose `CardDefinition` is not `Complete`, and the reason
given in the source is exactly the one that matters here:

```rust
    /// The definition exists but is marked `Inert`, `Partial`, or `KnownWrong`
    /// (see `cards::Completeness`). Such a card would take actions the rules
    /// engine never emits, or emit actions the card does not have, producing a
    /// state history that cannot be correctly rewound. Surfaced here, at deck
    /// build, rather than silently misbehaving on turn 6.
```
— `crates/engine/src/rules/commander.rs:46-50`, enforced at `commander.rs:232`.

An engine that picks a player's target, keeps or bottoms their scried cards, or discards
their cleanup card produces precisely "a state history that cannot be correctly rewound",
because the history records a decision no player made. DP-INV is therefore the same
invariant Architecture Invariant 9 already asserts, applied to *choices* rather than to
*abilities*.

**The gate is narrower than the invariant.** `crates/engine/tests/core/effect_choose_gate.rs`
(SR-33) bars exactly three DSL variants from `Complete`:

| gate test | variant barred |
|---|---|
| `no_complete_def_uses_the_choose_stub` (`:84`) | `Effect::Choose` |
| `no_complete_def_uses_the_may_pay_or_else_stub` (`:109`) | `Effect::MayPayOrElse` |
| `no_complete_def_uses_the_add_mana_choice_stub` (`:149`) | `Effect::AddManaChoice` |

Every other auto-chosen decision ships `Complete`. That is the hole this audit measures.

---

## 2. Classification and method

### 2.1 The taxonomy (from the task brief)

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| **A** | Player-hooked: the choice rides a `Command` field and the handler reads it and acts on it. |
| **B** | Deterministic auto-fallback: the engine picks legally, without player input. Legal game state, zero agency. |
| **C** | Gated/stubbed: the decision is unimplemented and the corpus gate keeps affected cards out of `Complete`. |
| **D** | Missing or wrong vs CR: the behaviour diverges from the rules, or a hook exists that is never honoured. |

### 2.2 Evidence standard

A site is class **A** only if the choice was traced from a `Command` field, through
`process_command`'s dispatcher, into the handler line that consumes it. "The `Command` has a
field" was never accepted as evidence — three findings below (`face_down_kind`,
`ChooseDungeonRoom`, `Command::OrderReplacements` in reply to a `WouldDraw` prompt) are
exactly cases where a field or command exists and is discarded.

Every CR number cited here was looked up against `.scryfall-cache/MagicCompRules.txt` via the
mtg-rules MCP. Two corrections to the task brief resulted:

- **Scry is CR 701.22, not 701.19.** CR 701.19 is *Regenerate*. Surveil is **CR 701.25**.
- **CR 602.2e does not exist.** `abilities.rs:1384` cites it; CR 602.2 has only 602.2a/b.
  See finding **DP-1**.

Line numbers were verified by reading the files, and the four delegated research legs were
spot-checked against source before their claims were adopted. One agent-reported count was
wrong and is corrected here: `Effect::MayPayThenEffect` appears in **11** effectively-`Complete`
defs, not 12 — `mana_vault`, `temur_sabertooth`, `call_of_the_ring`, `boggart_shenanigans`,
`roil_elemental`, `ezuri_stalker_of_spheres`, `ruthless_technomancer` and `vampire_gourmand`
are `partial` or `inert`.

### 2.3 Corpus-impact method

Counts below come from a regex sweep over `crates/card-defs/src/defs/*.rs`, **excluding
`defs/mod.rs`** (the module file, which is caught by the glob but is not a card) — 1,804 def
files. A def is "effectively `Complete`" if it says `Completeness::Complete` **or** carries no
`completeness:` line at all (the DSL default) — **1,139 files, exactly matching
`tools/authoring-report.py`.**

This is an *approximation*: it is a source regex, not the serde walk `effect_choose_gate.rs`
uses, so it will miss a variant reached only through a deeply nested generated ability and
will over-count a variant that appears only in a comment. (`Effect::Choose` is the live example
of both traps at once: the bare string appears in 119 files, **all** of them prose in doc
comments; actual code use — `Effect::Choose {` — is zero.) Word boundaries matter too:
`Discover\b` is the mechanic (CR 701.57) and deliberately does not match the card name
*Kindred Discovery*, which is unrelated and `inert` besides.

**Method, so §10's re-derivation instruction is actionable.** Each §3.1 row is a regex over the
file's source text; a def counts once per row it matches. Nineteen rows are a plain match on the
variant name as written in the table. Two are compound predicates on the same variant and must
both be included in the union:

- *targeted triggered ability* = `AbilityDefinition::Triggered` **and** `targets:\s*vec!\[\s*TargetRequirement::`
- *modal triggered ability* = `AbilityDefinition::Triggered` **and** `modes:\s*Some`

Runnable script: `scratchpad/count-classb.py` from this task's session
(`/tmp/claude-1000/-home-skydude-projects-scutemob--worktrees-scutemob-148/…/scratchpad/`).

## 3. Corpus impact

### 3.1 `Complete` defs containing at least one auto-chosen decision

> **SUPERSEDED (PB-DP10, `scutemob-158`).** The counts below are a 2026-07-26 source-regex
> estimate. The authoritative, machine-computed numbers are printed on every `cargo test` by
> `crates/engine/tests/core/decision_gate.rs::decision_site_reconciliation_report`
> (`core::decision_gate::decision_site_reconciliation_report`), enumerated from `all_cards()`
> per SR-36 rather than grepped, and ratcheted against silent growth by
> `no_complete_def_introduces_an_unrecorded_auto_chosen_decision` (T4) +
> `auto_chosen_complete_union_is_ratcheted` (T6). **Two CR cites below were wrong and are
> corrected here**: `DiscardCards … (CR 701.8)` — CR 701.8 is *Destroy*; discard is CR
> **701.9**, and CR **701.9b** is the load-bearing sentence PB-DP7 already used correctly for
> the cleanup discard. `PutOnLibrary … (CR 701.20)` — CR 701.20 is *Reveal*; there is no "put
> on library" keyword action, and the governing rules are CR **608.2d** (which cards) + CR
> **401.4** (their order). The `WheelDraw` needle has **no runtime key at all** — it is a
> *type* (`Effect::WheelHand { draw: WheelDraw }` serializes as `"draw": {"Fixed": …}`), not a
> variant of the walked tree; the `WheelHand` row is **NO-DECISION** (the whole hand is
> discarded, so the pick order the sibling `DiscardCards` row worries about is unobservable),
> not AUTO. As measured 2026-07-27 (PROTOCOL 31 / HASH 68, `mtg-engine` on this branch): 4 rows
> are **SERVED** (`triggered_targets` 77, `search_library` 73, `scry` 16, `surveil` 8), 2 are
> **GATED** at a hard zero by `effect_choose_gate.rs` (`choose_stub`, `may_pay_or_else`), 1 is
> **NO-DECISION** (`wheel_hand`), and the remaining 15 rows are **AUTO-CHOSEN** — see the live
> test output for exact per-row counts. The still-auto union (this table's non-served rows,
> unioned rather than summed) is **97** `Complete` defs, frozen in `decision_gate.rs`'s
> `BASELINE`; the all-rows union (this row's own 277 analogue, unioned across all 22 rows
> including the served ones) is **267**.
>
> **This gate is bounded, and the bound is worse than it sounds.** Every row above is a
> predicate over a *DSL variant name*, so it can only see a decision someone actually
> encoded as a decision-bearing variant. A card whose "may"/"choose" was dropped at
> authoring time — never expressed as `MayPayThenEffect`, `Choose`, a mode, or anything
> else — produces a serialized tree with no trace of the choice and hits zero rows,
> forever. This is not hypothetical: PB-DP10's own closing review (2026-07-27) found
> Smuggler's Copter authored as an unconditional `Sequence(DrawCards, DiscardCards)` for a
> printed "you **may** draw a card" (CR 118.12) — it appears in `BASELINE` at all only
> because of the incidental `DiscardCards`. **That class is strictly worse than any row in
> this table**, because a recorded auto-choice is at least a legal outcome, while a dropped
> "may" is not. See **OOS-DP10-9**.
>
> **Per-row reconciliation, audit estimate vs. the gate's measured count (fix-review
> cycle, 2026-07-27):**

> **277 of 1,139 effectively-`Complete` defs — 24.3% — contain at least one decision the
> engine makes for the player.**

The four zero-`Complete` rows at the bottom are **not** a control group that "gets there two
different ways", as this table originally claimed. `MayPayOrElse` and `Effect::Choose` are
genuinely held out by the SR-33 gate, which works exactly as designed for the variants it
names. But `AddManaFilterChoice` and `TheRingTemptsYou` were held at zero by **nothing but
hand-authoring discipline** — the SR-33 gate bars the key `AddManaChoice`, a different serde
key than `AddManaFilterChoice`, and does not reach it at all. PB-DP10's `T7`
(`hard_zero_rows_have_no_complete_defs`) converts both into machine-checked hard zeros at zero
engine cost. The gate previously did not name the other seventeen rows at all; PB-DP10 closes
that gap at the corpus-measurement level (not the engine level — see the PB-DP10 row in §8).

> **New row filed by PB-DX23 (`scutemob-201`, 2026-08-05), NON-DSL — `OOS-DX2-7`.** The
> stale-`PendingDraw` auto-discharge at `rules/replacement.rs::perform_one_draw` (CR 702.52a /
> 614.11a) is **AUTO-CHOSEN**: the engine, not the player, declines an outstanding dredge (or
> CR 616.1) offer the instant another draw arrives for the same player. **`Complete` defs
> reachable: 1** — `golgari_grave_troll`, the corpus's only dredge def. **This row cannot
> appear in the table above, and that is not a gate bug.** `decision_site_walk.rs` /
> `decision_gate.rs` walk card-def `Effect`/`Condition` DSL variant names over `all_cards()`;
> dredge is a `KeywordAbility`, reached through none of those variants, so it is invisible to
> the walk **by construction**. This is a fresh instance of **OOS-DP10-9** (a decision the DSL
> never encoded as a decision-bearing variant, so the machine-computed table can never see it,
> no matter how faithfully the card is authored) — and, per that seed's own framing, "strictly
> worse than any row in this table," since even a recorded auto-choice is at least visible;
> this one is invisible to the very instrument built to find it.
>
> **Where it structurally belongs, and why it is filed here instead.** §3.2 immediately below
> is titled "decisions that need no card at all" — six findings reachable in *every* game
> regardless of decklist (priority, mulligan, cleanup discard, damage assignment, trigger
> ordering, mana-pool spend order). `OOS-DX2-7` is the opposite shape: it cannot arise at all
> without a specific card (`golgari_grave_troll`) reaching a graveyard first, so it does not
> belong in §3.2 either. It is filed here, in §3.1, because §3.1 is this document's
> corpus-impact ledger — the place a reader checking "how many `Complete` defs carry an
> auto-chosen decision" would look first — and a NON-DSL row the machine-computed table cannot
> carry is exactly the blind spot this section's own "this gate is bounded" paragraph (above)
> already warns about in the abstract. This row makes that warning concrete with a real,
> `Complete`, deck-legal card.
>
> **Status after PB-DX23: still open, recorded not closed.** PB-DX23 (`scutemob-201`) made the
> dredge offer *answerable* — `LegalAction::ChooseDredge` now exists end to end for both the
> bot and the human browser seat. It did **not** make the auto-discharge *stop being an
> engine-made decision*. A player who does not answer before their next draw event still has
> the offer answered for them, by the engine, at a moment of the engine's choosing rather than
> theirs — and the discharged draw is not outcome-neutral (it takes the top of the library at
> the moment of the *later* draw, not the original offer, so an intervening scry/shuffle/mill
> changes what the discharge draws). **Extended by the review fix cycle (finding E5, `scutemob-201`
> 2026-08-05): this auto-discharge reaches the TAIL of an answered multi-draw sequence too, not
> only its head.** `resolve_declined_pending_draw`'s own `perform_one_draw` call for THIS draw is
> unconditionally `false` (no re-decision), but the tail it then resumes through
> `perform_remaining_draws` is auto-declined WHOLE when the resume came from the implicit
> stale-entry discharge (`tail_offers_dredge: false`) — an asymmetry against the answered-path
> tail, which DOES get re-offered dredge on each of its own draws (`resolve_pending_draw`'s
> `true`, see `perform_remaining_draws`'s doc). Zero corpus reach today, same as the head case.
> Full finding text: **OOS-DX2-7** in the §8 seed table, and the "Dredge offer's implicit decline
> (stale-entry discharge)" row in §4.10 (Replacement-effect ordering), which this paragraph
> supplements rather than duplicates.

### 3.2 Decisions that need no card at all

Six findings are in core turn structure and combat and are reachable in **every** game
regardless of decklist: priority after casting (**DP-1**), the mulligan (**DP-2**), cleanup
discard (**DP-3**), combat damage assignment (**DP-13**), same-controller trigger ordering
(**DP-14**), and the mana-pool spend order (**DP-26**).

### 4.6 Triggered-ability targets (CR 603.3d)

**Class B.** `rules/abilities.rs:7174-7500`, inside `flush_pending_triggers`
(`abilities.rs:6950`). For `PendingTriggerKind::Normal` and `CardDefETB`, the ability's
`TargetRequirement`s are read from layer-resolved characteristics and satisfied by
first-match scan:

```rust
            // CR 603.3d: For CardDef-based triggered abilities (Normal / CardDefETB),
            // look up the target requirements from the ability definition and
            // auto-select legal targets using deterministic first-match fallback.
            // If any required target has no legal candidate, skip this trigger.
```
— `abilities.rs:7178-7181`

Exact rules by requirement kind:

- `TargetPlayer` / `TargetCreatureOrPlayer` / `TargetAny` / `TargetPlayerOrPlaneswalker`:
  **first non-lost, non-conceded opponent in `turn_order`, else the controller**
  (`abilities.rs:7249-7270`).
- `TargetOpponent`: first active opponent, **never** self-fallback (`:7276-7291`).
- Graveyard-card requirements: first match in `state.objects` iteration order, i.e.
  **ascending `ObjectId`** (`:7293-7362`).
- `UpToN`: contributes **zero** targets for a permanent inner requirement (`:7419-7422`).
- Battlefield permanents: first match in ascending `ObjectId` (`:7425+`), correctly filtered
  through `layers::expect_characteristics` and `validate_target_protection`
  (`:7434-7450` — CR 613.1f, so Humility is respected).

This is **CR-compliant**: protection/hexproof/shroud are honoured and a requirement with no
legal candidate removes the ability from the stack, exactly as CR 603.3d directs. It is not
a rules violation — it is a total loss of agency across **84 effectively-`Complete` defs**.
Modal triggers are the same shape: `abilities.rs:8398-8405` sets `modes_chosen = vec![0]`
(CR 603.3c), affecting 5 `Complete` defs.

**No hook exists.** The `Command` enum (`rules/command.rs:19-638`) has no trigger-target
variant, and `rules/events.rs` has no `TriggerTargetRequired` event.

Effective rule: **ascending source `ObjectId`, then ability index, then sweep-call order** |

No `Command` and no `GameEvent` for trigger ordering exists.

Repaired to `new_with_kicker` (`scutemob-154`) |
| Intervening-if at **queue time** | ~~D~~ → **A** | **CLOSED by PB-DP6 (`scutemob-154`).** All **14** card-def trigger-queue sites now gate on the intervening-if via one shared helper, `abilities::carddef_intervening_if_holds_at_queue_time` (`:9137`), paired with an exhaustive, no-wildcard `effects::condition_is_queue_time_evaluable`. The original cell was wrong in three ways: (1) the cites were stale by 300-400 lines (`replacement.rs:1446-1456` → `:1838`; `abilities.rs:6910-6916` → `:7018`), filed as **OOS-DP6-8**; (2) *"only two paths check it"* conflated two different mechanisms — the runtime `Option<InterveningIf>` (a 2-variant enum, `check_intervening_if`) was already gated at all 13 of its sites and was never the gap; DP-15 is only about the card-def `Option<Condition>`; (3) the audited roster of 3 sites was a fifth of the real one. Remaining known holes are **seeded, not open-ended**: OOS-DP6-1 (condition dropped by lowering — fails at *both* ends, needs a HASH bump), OOS-DP6-2 (the one deliberately-ungated Category-C site), OOS-DP6-5 / OOS-DP6-9 (`TurnFaceUp` and Haunt lack the *resolution* half) |

The queue-time gap produced a **false-positive trigger**: condition false when the ability
would go on the stack, true at resolution ⇒ this engine fired, real Magic never triggers.
The false-negative direction was handled by the resolution check. **Both halves now hold**
(CR 603.4 requires the check in both places, and PB-DP6 retained the resolution re-check
rather than treating the new gate as making it redundant — state changes between queueing
and resolution, so it does not).

**The framing above missed the third possibility, and it is the worst one.** A condition can
be *dropped entirely* rather than merely checked late: when a card-def triggered ability is
lowered into a runtime `TriggeredAbilityDef`, `intervening_if` is hardcoded `None` because
the two types are different, so the condition is checked in **neither** place. Confirmed by
execution at PB-DP6 close-out: this makes `aurelia_the_warleader` — `Complete` and
deck-legal — an **unbounded infinite-combat loop**. See **OOS-DP6-1**, which is the highest
open item this audit has produced outside Tier 0.

### 4.9 Resolution-time choices

There is **no resolution-time decision channel at all**. `execute_effect_inner` returns `()`
and cannot suspend; `GameState` has six `pending_*` fields and none of them is an
effect-choice; the `Command` enum has no general `MakeChoice`.

> **SUPERSEDED for the first three rows by PB-DP9 (`scutemob-157`).** There IS a
> resolution-time decision channel now: `GameState.pending_effect_choice` +
> `GameEvent::EffectChoiceRequired` -> `Command::AnswerEffectChoice`, backed by an
> **abort-and-replay** continuation for `resolve_top_of_stack` (clone at entry; an effect
> that needs an unanswered choice records the question and returns; the wrapper restores the
> clone wholesale and emits the question; the answer is banked and the resolution re-runs from
> the top). `execute_effect_inner` still returns `()` and still cannot suspend — that premise
> was correct and is exactly why the mechanism is an abort rather than a pause. **The channel
> generalises to every remaining row in this table for the cost of one `EffectChoiceQuestion`
> / `EffectChoiceAnswer` variant pair and zero new plumbing** — no new `Command`, no new
> `GameEvent`, no new `LegalAction`, no new `DecisionKind`, no new admission-gate entry. That
> reuse, not the three effects themselves, is PB-DP9's real deliverable.

## 5. Ranked B/D findings

One row — **DP-32** — is marked `A*`. Its *choice* is class A (honoured, never defaulted); it
is listed here because the surrounding machinery is not, and a reader ranking work items needs
to see it next to the rest. It is the only non-B/D row in this section.

Ranking dimension is **human-play impact**: how often a human at one seat of a 4-player
Commander game hits the site × how far the engine's pick is from what a player would choose ×
whether it ships in `Complete` cards or in core rules.

> **PB-DP10 note (`scutemob-158`).** The still-open class-B rows with a card-def corpus
> presence are now **baselined by the gate, not closed**: their `Complete` defs are frozen
> in `decision_gate.rs`'s `BASELINE` and ratcheted against silent growth (T4/T6), but the
> class does not change. This covers **DP-16** (sacrifice/discard edicts →
> `sacrifice_permanents` / `discard_cards`), **DP-17** (Proliferate → `proliferate`),
> **DP-18** (`CounterUnlessPays` → `counter_unless_pays`), **DP-19** (`MayPayThenEffect` →
> `may_pay_then_effect`), part of **DP-20** (Discover → `discover`; Cascade and
> `PlayExiledCard` have no dedicated §3.1 row), and part of **DP-25** (`ChangeTargets` →
> `change_targets`; ring-bearer → `the_ring_tempts_you`, held at a hard zero by `T7`, not
> baselined — no `Complete` def uses it; Riot/Exploit/Hideaway/legend rule have no dedicated
> row). **DP-13, DP-14, DP-26 and DP-31 have no corresponding §3.1 row at all** (combat
> damage assignment, trigger ordering, and cost/redirect micro-choices are global engine

### Tier 0 — correctness class: the engine's behaviour diverges from the CR

Four of the five are class **D** — wrong, not merely un-consulted. **DP-3 is class B**, and
sits here because it is the only decision in the whole audit with *no `Command` at all* on a
turn-based action every human hits.

Reachability differs from severity and the two are deliberately not the same list: DP-1, DP-2
and DP-3 are core-reachable (no card required), while DP-4 needs one of three specific
`Complete` cards in the deck and DP-5 needs two `WouldDraw` replacements on the board. The
core-reachable set is §3.2's six.

**Correction (PB-DP5, `scutemob-153`):** DP-5's reachability was in fact **zero**, not merely
narrow — **no card in the 1,804-def corpus registers a `WouldDraw` replacement at all**, so
"needs two on the board" could never be satisfied from a legal deck. That does not change its
Tier-0 placement (the defect is in engine machinery every future draw-replacement card would
route through, and its planning surfaced **OOS-DP5-7**, which *is* live), but it is a caution
about this table's method: "which cards does it need" was answered from the finding's shape
rather than by enumerating the corpus, and the enumeration was cheap.

## 6. What the audit did **not** cover

Stated so a re-audit knows where the edges are.

- **Card-by-card verification.** The corpus counts in §3.1 were a regex sweep, not the serde
  walk `effect_choose_gate.rs` uses — treat the original table as a magnitude, not an exact
  roster. **PB-DP10 (`scutemob-158`) superseded this**: `crates/engine/tests/core/
  decision_gate.rs::decision_site_reconciliation_report` now enumerates all 22 rows from
  `all_cards()` and prints exact numbers on every `cargo test`. Two mechanisms explain most
  of the drift from the original estimate to the measured numbers: the compound rows
  (`triggered_targets` / `modal_trigger`) are qualified per-`AbilityDefinition::Triggered`-node
  in the gate but were a file-level regex conjunction in the original sweep (which over- or
  under-counts depending on whether a def's other abilities happen to share the file), and the
  unit-variant rows (`proliferate`, `the_ring_tempts_you`) require string-value matching that
  no walk before this batch performed (see the PB-DP10 row in §8). **Two more mechanisms,
  found by PB-DP10's closing fix-review cycle** (2026-07-27; full per-row table in §3.1's
  superseded note): (iii) the audit's regex counted a variant name appearing inside a
  `Completeness` note string (a comment-like field the serde walk cannot see) as a real hit —
  the whole of the `connive` 2→1 and `put_on_library` 3→1 deltas; (iv) the audit's original
  row 4 bundled two runtime predicates (`DiscardCards` and `WheelHand`) under one count, and
  the split is exact: `discard_cards` 13 + `wheel_hand` 10 = 23. Three further deltas
  (`search_library` 74→73, `may_pay_then_effect` 11→10, `modal_trigger` 5→4) are left
  **unexplained, ±1, within regex noise** rather than assigned a mechanism this suite has not
  verified — this suite has published a plausible-sounding roster as fact and been wrong three
  times before (PB-DP6's 3-vs-14, PB-DP8's 84-vs-77, PB-DP9's 74/16/8-vs-69/16/7-vs-73/16/8),
  and an honest gap beats another plausible story.
- **The simulator's `StubProvider` gaps** (Adventure, alt-costs, modes, convoke/improvise/delve)
  are move-generator limits, not engine decision-surface gaps, and are already catalogued as
  M11-local risk R4.
- **Whether each class-B tie-break is the *worst* choice.** This audit establishes what the
  engine picks; it does not model how much equity a player loses. That is the ranking input
  §5 approximates by frequency and by "distance from a sensible pick".
- **Deferred subsystems** already tracked elsewhere: Battle (OOS retriage plan), Banding
  (ability-coverage doc), P2P/hidden-information (M10).

## 7. OOS-M11 seed assessment

Explicitly requested. **`memory/primitives/rider-seed-triage-2026-07-19.md` was not modified**
— that queue is paused at PB-RS4 and belongs to the coordinator.

### OOS-M11-1 — mulligan no-shuffle: **CONFIRMED as filed; covers one of two defects**

The seed itself is exact. The **§8 risk table, row R2** — the row that proposes the id
`OOS-M11-1`, at `m11-session-plan.md:800` as committed at the time of this audit and `:814` in
that worktree's working copy, so grep for `OOS-M11-1` rather than trusting the line — reads
"A mulligan today returns the same hand — a live-wrong rules path (CR 103.5 requires a
shuffle)", and this audit confirms it verbatim. (The plan's §1 fact 1 hedges to
"near-identical"; the seed does not, and the seed is right.)

`Zone::insert` on an ordered zone is `push_back`
(`crates/card-types/src/state/zone.rs:109`) and `Zone::top` is `v.last()` (`:159-164`), so the
seven cards moved hand→library are the seven cards drawn back. No RNG is invoked — the engine
*does* have a deterministic seeded PRNG (`effects/mod.rs:8697-8703`, `:3049`, `:3148`, seeded
from `state.timestamp_counter`), and `handle_take_mulligan` calls none of it. The emitted
`GameEvent::LibraryShuffled` is a phantom, which is an Architecture Invariant 4 problem in its
own right ("events are the single source of truth for what happened").

**Widen the seed.** What the seed does *not* cover is a second, independent, cheaper defect on
the same command pair — this audit's genuinely new contribution here: `handle_keep_hand`
(`rules/commander.rs:886-890`) puts `cards_to_bottom` on the **top** of the library. That half
is a one-line `push_front` fix with no wire impact and it is a strictly-wrong rules path today.
Recommended rank: **Tier 0**, above every RS-queue item, on the same "live-wrong on a
`Complete` path" criterion that put OOS-RS-1 at the head of the RS queue.

**CLOSED by PB-DP2 (`scutemob-150`, 2026-07-26) — including the widening this audit
recommended.** Both halves shipped together in `rules/commander.rs`: `handle_take_mulligan`
now runs a real seeded Fisher-Yates `Zone::shuffle` before the `LibraryShuffled` event and
the draws (so the event is no longer a phantom), and `handle_keep_hand` now uses
`move_object_to_bottom_of_zone` (`push_front`) so bottomed cards land on the bottom. The seed
is `state.timestamp_counter` — the same deterministic PRNG source this section pointed at —
so replay determinism (SR-9b) holds and **no wire change was needed** (PROTOCOL 27 / HASH 63
unmoved), falsifying §8's HASH-bump prediction for the (b) half. 4 fail-before/pass-after
probes in `crates/engine/tests/rules/commander.rs`; tests 3,721 → 3,725.

### OOS-M11-2 — mana solver: **CONFIRMED, correctly ranked low, and it should not enter the primitive queue**

> **⚠️ BOTH HALVES DESCRIBED BELOW ARE CLOSED (SIM-2, `scutemob-176`, 2026-08-02), and one of
> them was worse than this section says.** The pool half closed at the solver
> (`solve_mana_payment_with_pool` subtracts the pool in `ManaPool::can_spend`'s own order and
> solves the residual, so `LocalGame::auto_tap_commands_for` no longer compensates with an
> all-or-nothing check that solved for the whole printed cost). The layer half closed by
> `gather_sources` calling `calculate_characteristics` — and the example this section reaches
> for is the reason it sat: **a Cryptolith-Rite-granted mana ability is exotic, and the live
> instance was a face-down permanent** (CR 707.2 — `layers.rs` clears `mana_abilities`
> outright), which the S8 scripted playthrough hit on seed 42 the moment source selection
> moved. Also closed, and not named here at all: the solver counted one mana per SOURCE
> rather than per mana produced, so Sol Ring was one mana and a `{2}` spell it pays for was
> never offered (playtest **F4**). What is left of `OOS-M11-2` is cost *modifiers* (no
> Thalia-style increase, no reduction) and CR 106.12 restricted mana. The line cites below are
> pre-SIM-2 and no longer resolve; the paragraph is kept verbatim as the record of what was
> believed at the time.

Both halves verified. `crates/simulator/src/mana_solver.rs` contains **zero** references to
`mana_pool` (so a human who taps manually and then casts is over-tapped), and it reads
`obj.characteristics.mana_abilities` directly (`mana_solver.rs:44`) rather than
`calculate_characteristics`, so a Cryptolith-Rite-granted or animated-land mana ability is
invisible to it.

But this is **simulator-side**, and the engine's own payment paths are layer-correct and
authoritative — `solve_mana_payment` returns a `Vec<Command>` of real `TapForMana` values that
`process_command` then judges. It cannot produce a wrong game state; it produces a wrong
*suggestion*. It belongs in M11-local (Session 3 item 7 already fixes the pool half), **not**
in the primitive queue, which is for engine correctness. Recommended rank: below every class-D
finding in §5.

> **Rider added by PB-DP4 (`scutemob-152`).** The attack-tax debit makes the pool-blindness
> cost real in combat too: a bot that taps for the tax and then has that mana actually *spent*
> will over-tap on its next action, because the solver never reads the pool. Still an
> M11-local Session 3 item, not a primitive-queue item — but it now costs the bot mana rather
> than only a suggestion. See also **OOS-DP4-8** (the provider offers attack targets whose tax
> the player cannot pay at all).

> **CONFIRMED by `scutemob-159` (2026-07-31), the seed re-rank.** Both halves re-checked at
> source: `crates/simulator/src/mana_solver.rs` still contains **zero** occurrences of
> `mana_pool`, and still reads `obj.characteristics.mana_abilities` directly at `:35` rather
> than `calculate_characteristics`. `memory/m11-session-plan.md:914` (risk R3) already assigns
> the pool half to Session 3 item 7. **This section's exclusion stands and is now recorded as a
> queue decision, not just a recommendation**: OOS-M11-2 is explicitly listed in
> `memory/primitives/seed-rerank-2026-07-27.md` §1d ("NOT the primitive queue — owned
> elsewhere") so a future dispatcher does not re-rank it. The reasoning is the one this section
> gives: the engine's own payment paths are layer-correct and authoritative, and
> `solve_mana_payment` returns a `Vec<Command>` that `process_command` then judges, so it cannot
> produce a wrong game state — only a wrong suggestion.

### OOS-M11-4 (né OOS-M11-3; renumbered — ID taken by scutemob-147's fuzzer-nondeterminism seed) — triggered-ability targets: **CONFIRMED; reclassify B, not D** — **CLOSED by PB-DP8 (`scutemob-156`, 2026-07-26)**

> **CLOSED.** `Command::ChooseTriggerTargets` + `GameEvent::TriggerTargetChoiceRequired` +
> `GameState.pending_trigger_targets` suspend `flush_pending_triggers` mid-batch and resume it
> when the trigger's controller answers (PROTOCOL 28 → **29**, HASH 65 → **66**). The compliant
> CR 603.3d fallback is preserved verbatim as `abilities::default_trigger_targets`, which the
> *caller* submits as a real `Command` — the engine still never auto-picks on a decision path
> and still knows nothing about seat kind (Architecture Invariant 1). Roster **77**, not 84.
> Two corrections this closure forced, both recorded in §8's PB-DP8 row: an `UpToN` slot was
> not "contributing 0 targets" but **removing the whole trigger**, and the four guarded call
> sites needed an explicit priority-grant obligation on the pending entry.

Verified at `rules/abilities.rs:7174-7500` (stale — the arm was at `:7308-7798` when PB-DP8
re-verified it). The fallback is **CR 603.3d-compliant**: it uses layer-resolved characteristics
(`layers::expect_characteristics`, `:7434` → really `:7571`), honours protection/hexproof/shroud
(`validate_target_protection`, `:7438-7450` → really `:7573-7582`), never self-targets a
`TargetOpponent` requirement (`:7272-7291` → really `:7410-7425`), and removes the trigger from
the stack when a required slot has no legal candidate — exactly what CR 603.3d directs. **All
four claims re-verified true on the PB-DP8 branch.**

**One exception PB-DP8 found and this section did not:** the compliance claim holds for every
*required* slot and fails for an **`UpToN` ("up to N target ...") slot**. That arm returned
`None`, and the surrounding loop reads `None` as "no legal target" and removes the whole trigger.
CR 601.2c makes zero targets a legal announcement for "up to", so CR 603.3d's removal clause
never applies — Sword of Sinew and Steel and Elder Deep-Fiend (both `Complete`) had never once
put their trigger on the stack. Fixed by PB-DP8 as a consequence of making `optional` mean
anything at all.

So this is not (mostly) a rules violation. It is a **total loss of agency on 77 effectively-`Complete`
defs** — the largest single-site agency loss in the corpus after tutors. Recommended rank:
**top of Tier 1**, immediately below the Tier-0 correctness items, and it is the flagship
motivator for the pending-decision work in §8 because it is the first finding that *requires* a
new `Command` (and therefore a PROTOCOL bump). **Shipped as PB-DP8, `scutemob-156`.**

Also, for whoever writes DP-8/DP-9's tests: answering via `process_command` **completes and advances** in one round-trip when nothing else is pending, so a test that needs to hold the intermediate moment still must call the handler directly (PB-DP7's second-pause and out-of-step tests are the worked examples). **A fourth lesson came from the closing `/review`, and it is about the block's blast radius rather than the block itself: a gate that stops the engine also stops every loop built on top of it.** The TUI's auto-pass loop spun on `PassPriority` every 50ms against a blocked human seat — its stop condition required the main phase, and the rejection was swallowed into a status message — so the key that would clear the block was unreachable. The derivation that transfers is "the guard set is every statement that executes after the suspending call, within the same `process_command` invocation". (2) **A guard that returns early inherits a debt.** Each of the four sites was about to grant priority; simply returning leaves a resumed game with nobody holding priority — a hang. The plan did not say who grants it, and it cannot be inferred at resume time (the fifth call site owes nothing). Fixed with an explicit `resume_site: FlushResumeSite` on the pending entry (a `bool` named `grant_priority_on_resume` at implement close; widened by the fix cycle when review Finding 4 showed the priority grant was not the only thing those sites owed -- the CR 726 loop check and the cleanup ratchet had to be reproduced too), set by the guards and inherited when the same batch suspends again. **Any future blocking decision taken mid-turn-based-action needs the same question asked.** (3) **The pending state is an `Option`, not the `Vector` PB-DP7's §1.5 predicted.** CR 603.3b's batch is answered as a *sequence*, and "answered as a sequence" is precisely what makes the outstanding set a singleton; the plurality lives in a `remaining: Vector<PendingTrigger>` **inside** the entry, which is what it actually is — the un-flushed tail of one batch. (4) **`LocalGame` had a latent variant-blindness bug PB-DP7's review did not catch**: `advance()` read the liveness-filtered predicate correctly and then hard-coded `DecisionKind::CleanupDiscard`, so a second variant would have handed a browser client the wrong picker. Three transferable rules: (i) **when a guard SKIPS work, enumerate what that work was going to do and name where each part is picked up** — the gate's source comment asserted the resume would grant priority, and for the most common resume site it does not; (ii) **a test that constructs a hazardous state and does not assert against it is worse than no test**, because it reads as coverage (`test_dp8_foreign_concede_does_not_step_over_the_suspended_batch` built the exact 4-step deadlock and never looked at `priority_holder`); (iii) **a debt-carrying pending entry needs a merge rule, not a choose-one rule** — the CR 800.4d reap discharged a stale debt inside the caller's own flush and double-granted priority (OOS-DP8-13). Also closed: the engine could refuse its own default answer for two mutually-distinct slots (SR-38 hole, OOS-DP8-4 narrowed), the script harness's pump-skip was step-local and kind-blind (OOS-DP8-14), and the ESM criterion-5545 test was vacuous — it hashed a state it had cloned INTO the call, and now drives `handle_choose_trigger_targets(&mut state, ..)` once per rejection class, proven non-vacuous by a mutate-before-validate probe. Two concedes in a row under one suspended batch (P2 concedes as holder while P1's announcement is open, then P1 concedes instead of answering) reproduced the identical unrecoverable deadlock. Fixed with an unconditional backstop at the **end** of `handle_concede` rather than at the review's suggested site immediately after the drop (there it would preempt the existing advance on the ordinary concede path, where `next_priority_player() == None` owes `handle_all_passed` per MR-M2-03, not a grant to the active player). **The transferable rule (iv): a choke point placed on the "answered" path is not a choke point — enumerate every exit from a blocking decision, and departure is always one of them.** And (v), the meta-lesson: **this was the THIRD time in one batch that a source comment asserted a property the code did not have** — the pre-fix gate comment, its replacement ("nothing is skipped here that is not picked up there", false for the departure exit), and `default_trigger_targets`' "one exception" doc (which named the wrong failure mode for the both-slots-forced half). OOS-DP7-11's lesson generalises: a comment that *justifies* skipping work is a claim about reachability, and reachability claims need the same enumeration a match arm does. That is **impossible**: `resolve_top_of_stack` **pops** the stack object at `resolution.rs:39-42`, before a single effect runs, so nothing living on the stack object can carry a continuation for effect execution. What shipped instead is an **abort-and-replay**: `resolve_top_of_stack` clones the state at entry; an effect that needs an unanswered choice records the *question* and returns; the wrapper **restores the clone wholesale** (the stack object is back, no card has moved, no event happened) and returns exactly one event, the question; the answer is banked on `GameState` and the resolution is re-run **from the top**, retracing the identical deterministic path and consuming the banked answer at the choice point. Five consequences, each worth carrying: (1) **there is no continuation data structure at all** — `Sequence`, `Conditional`, `ForEach`, `Repeat`, `MayPayThenEffect` and the per-player loops inside the asking effects are all handled with zero machinery, because the replay re-executes them, and re-deriving is *correct* rather than merely convenient since they are pure functions of a state the roll-back restored; (2) **the re-entrancy audit is three units, not twenty** — of the 17 production `execute_effect` callers, **15 are inside the single function `resolve_top_of_stack`**, one is `mana.rs:864` (gated by CR 605.1b/605.4a) and one is `replacement.rs:1964` (a literal `Effect::CreateToken`, provably unreachable); (3) **PB-DP8's hardest recurring bug class — "a guard that returns early inherits the obligation of the statements it skipped" — does not exist here**, because a total state restore has no debt: nothing was skipped, nothing happened. Its one residual, `handle_all_passed`'s two post-resolution statements, is factored into `finish_stack_resolution`; (4) **"the suspended object leaves the stack" is structurally unreachable** rather than a live hazard — the object was never removed and no admitted command removes stack objects; (5) the price is real and named: the resolution runs k+1 times for k choices (k is 1 or 2 across the whole corpus), one extra `GameState` clone per resolution (**measured: `full_turn_4p` 253 µs on `48353a36` vs 229 µs on-branch — no regression; `imbl` makes the clone a handful of refcount bumps**), and **SR-9b determinism becomes a RUNTIME requirement, not just a test one**. The detector for that last one is a question-equality check before consuming each banked answer. **Roster: 73 / 16 / 8 `Complete` (+25 / +3 / +1 non-`Complete`)**, enumerated from `all_cards()` per SR-36. **The batch's own first answer, 69 / 16 / 7, was ALSO wrong and is superseded here** (closing-review Finding 5): the shipped walk was a hand-written `match` that never descended into `AbilityDefinition::{Spell,Triggered,Activated}::modes`, never visited `AbilityDefinition::{SagaChapter,LoyaltyAbility}` or split-card halves at all, and omitted `Effect::CoinFlip` while its own doc comment claimed to cover it. Ten defs were missing (Binding the Old Gods, Evolution Charm, Insatiable Avarice, Thirsting Roots, Connive // Concoct `Complete`; Tooth and Nail, Urza's Saga, Retreat to Coralhelm, Wrenn and Seven, Kaito Bane of Nightmares non-`Complete`). The walk is now a **structurally complete serde walk of the serialized `CardDefinition`** — it visits every field of every variant at every depth by construction and cannot rot as the DSL grows. This is the third consecutive batch in which a roster number published as fact was wrong; the lesson is narrower than "enumerate, don't grep" — *a hand-written tree walk is a reachability claim and needs the same enumeration a match arm does*. **0 card-def edits, 0 completeness flips**, as predicted. **Three in-scope correctness fixes beyond the agency restoration**, all CR-derived and none of them in the plan's original brief: CR **701.22b** (`Scry 0` was emitting `Scried { count: 0 }`); CR **400.7** (scry-to-bottom renumbered every scried card and consumed `timestamp_counter`, the shuffle seed source — fixed with a `Zone::reposition_within` permutation, seed OOS-DP9-11 for the sweep); and CR 601.2c's principle applied to CR **701.23d** (a quantity-only search with exactly one candidate is determined and asks nothing). **The deliberate flip a reviewer should weigh hardest: the scry and surveil DEFAULTS are NOT status-quo-preserving.** PB-DP8 preserved its default byte-for-byte; PB-DP9 does that only for search (lowest `ObjectId`, zero churn) and flips scry/surveil to the **identity**. Both old defaults are CR-legal under "any number", but they are the systematically maximal-harm legal answer, and surveil-as-mill can contribute to a CR 704.5b deck-out. The cost is visible and was paid: **25 unit tests + 1 golden script** changed, every repair CR-justified, none by weakening an assertion. **A second deliberate deviation, from the PB-DP7/PB-DP8 precedent this time:** the three new `GameState` fields go into `public_state_hash` but **NOT** into `loop_detection.rs`'s mandatory-state fingerprint, because they GROW between replay *k* and replay *k+1* of the same resolution, so including them would make two structurally identical CR 726 positions fingerprint differently and could silently mask a mandatory loop. Recorded as **obligation (7)** on the `BlockingDecision` doc block, which is the first evidence that PB-DP8's six-obligation list generalises (it discharged 6/6 plus the new one). Tests 3,878 → **3,905** at implement close, → **3,906** after the fix cycle; seeds **OOS-DP9-1..16** filed below. **The closing review found two HIGHs, both on the concede exit** — the exit this suite keeps missing — and both are fixed: (1) the owner-concede test was VACUOUS (a 2-player fixture ends the game, so the discharge's resolve-and-drive half never executed while the test's doc claimed it did), rebuilt on a 3-player fixture with unconditional assertions; (2) a FOREIGN concede kept the answer bank bound to a pre-concede board, driving the replay's question-equality check into `debug_assert!(false)` — **a panic on a legal command sequence**, reproduced before fixing. The rule was re-derived rather than patched: the bank is valid only while the board the questions were asked against is the board the replay re-executes; `Concede` is the only other admitted command and it always mutates that board, so **any** concede now abandons the bank and re-drives, and the discharge moved to after every board mutation `handle_concede` performs. PROTOCOL 31 / HASH 68 unmoved by the fix cycle |
| **PB-DP10** | **gate widening** — the invariant-level fix for the whole PB-DP suite — **SHIPPED** (`scutemob-158`) | **none (test-only)** — prediction **confirmed**: PROTOCOL 31 / HASH 68 unmoved (`git diff --name-only main -- crates/engine/src crates/card-types/src crates/card-defs/src` empty), no card-def source edits, no completeness flips. Two new test-only files (`crates/engine/tests/core/decision_site_walk.rs`, `decision_gate.rs`, 18 new `#[test]`s after the fix-review cycle below), plus a rewire of `effect_choose_gate.rs`'s and `pb_rs1_roster_sweep.rs`'s object-key walks onto the canonical one (behavior-neutral, confirmed: 14/14 and 1/1 tests still pass with identical printed counts) and a doc-only note on `pb_dp9_effect_choice.rs::roster` | **Closes the queue this row headlines and marks the PB-DP suite COMPLETE.** The batch's headline technical finding, stated plainly: the serde walk every prior gate in this codebase used (`effect_choose_gate.rs`, `pb_rs1_roster_sweep.rs`, `pb_dp9_effect_choice.rs::roster`) matches OBJECT KEYS ONLY, and is therefore **blind to a unit `Effect` variant** — `Effect::Proliferate` and `Effect::TheRingTemptsYou` serialize to a bare JSON *string* (`serde_json::to_value(Effect::Proliferate) == Value::String("Proliferate")`, pinned directly by `T2`), not an object key, so a verbatim reuse of any prior walk would report **0** for `proliferate`'s 25 `Complete` defs while looking green — exactly the "gate reports success while checking nothing" failure mode OOS-DP7-11 was filed for. The new canonical walk (`decision_site_walk.rs::json_contains_variant`) matches BOTH shapes, with a `PROSE_FIELDS` denylist (`T3`) suppressing a false positive when a card's own oracle text, name, or a granted ability's `description` happens to spell a variant name exactly. **Measured taxonomy** (22 rows, not the original 21 — row 4 splits into `discard_cards` AUTO and `wheel_hand` NO-DECISION): **4 SERVED** (`triggered_targets` 77, `search_library` 73, `scry` 16, `surveil` 8 `Complete` defs — reproduced by value against PB-DP8's and PB-DP9's own published rosters, `T10`/`T11`), **2 GATED** (`choose_stub`, `may_pay_or_else`, both still 0 `Complete`), **1 NO-DECISION** (`wheel_hand`), **15 AUTO-CHOSEN**. Two of those fifteen — `add_mana_filter_choice` and `the_ring_tempts_you` — were **hand-maintained zeros held by nothing**: the SR-33 gate bars the key `AddManaChoice`, a different serde key than `AddManaFilterChoice`, and does not reach it at all; `T7` converts both into machine-checked hard zeros at zero engine cost. **Both unions**: the all-rows union (this section's own 277 analogue) is **267** `Complete` defs; the still-auto union — the rows with no hook at all, frozen in `decision_gate.rs`'s `BASELINE` — is **97**. **The gate, and its own bound.** `T4` (`no_complete_def_introduces_an_unrecorded_auto_chosen_decision`) fails on a `Complete` def hitting an `AutoChosen` row that is absent from `BASELINE` or present with a mismatched row set; `T6` ratchets the union count itself, closing the hole a per-def check alone cannot ("a new def slots into a freed seat"). **The fail-closed claim was proven END-TO-END, on a real card def, not only on a synthetic corpus**: `Effect::Proliferate` was temporarily added to `lightning_bolt.rs` (a `Complete` def that is not in `BASELINE`) and both `T4` and `T6` went red — `T4` naming the card, the row, the CR and the engine site (`Lightning Bolt is NOT in BASELINE but hits {"proliferate"}`), `T6` naming the union drift — then the def was restored and both went green. That is the acceptance criterion's actual claim ("fails on unmarked new instances") demonstrated by execution rather than by reading. **This does not close DP-INV** — the failure message says so explicitly, and the two legal exits are demote or record, never "implement the choice" (that needs the owning engine PB, DP-13..DP-31, still open). Also shipped: a source-scan collision inventory (`T12`, scoped to the plan's own cited cases — `Discover`'s accepted collision with `KeywordAbility::Discover`, the harmless `SearchLibrary`/`Scry`/`Surveil` twins in `state/stubs.rs`'s wire types structurally unreachable from `CardDefinition`, and the `ChooseColor`/`ChooseCreatureType` collision across `Effect` and `ReplacementModification` — the row most exposed to a silent count change and, until the fix-review cycle below, the only one left unguarded); a completeness proof that `PROSE_FIELDS` covers every `String`-typed field AND every newtype-over-`String` field (`SubType`, `CardId` — the only two such types in the crate) reachable from the DSL, across `card_definition.rs`, `game_object.rs`'s `TriggeredAbilityDef`, `state/types.rs`, `state/replacement_effect.rs` and `state/targeting.rs` (`T13`); a drift guard between `ROWS`'s `Gated` rows and `effect_choose_gate.rs`'s own bars (`T14`); and a residual-seed honesty check (`T16`). **And it can only see a decision the DSL encoded** — every row is a predicate over a variant name, so a "you may X. If you do, Y" authored as a bare `Effect::Sequence` (Smuggler's Copter, found in the fix-review cycle below) hits zero rows and passes; that class is strictly worse than the class this gate records, and this gate does not detect it (OOS-DP10-9). 18 new tests, tests 3,910 → **3,928**, PROTOCOL 31 / HASH 68 unmoved. Seeds **OOS-DP10-1..11** filed in §8.1; **closes OOS-DP7-7** (the §3.1 re-derivation is now computed, printed and ratcheted on every run, not merely owed). **Fix-review cycle (2026-07-27):** `pb-review-DP10.md` found 2 HIGH / 6 MEDIUM / 6 LOW; all 14 applied. Headline: `BASELINE`'s 97-entry freeze was populated mechanically and the plan §5.3 class-B/class-D triage was never performed against oracle text — a spot-check found two class-D members (Smuggler's Copter, Shambling Ghast; see OOS-DP10-8), so `BASELINE`'s doc comment and `T4`'s message now say so explicitly rather than implying a reviewed roster. `T4`'s non-vacuity probe was rewritten to actually drive the extracted `offenders()` function (previously it re-checked two predicates T1/T5 already covered and never exercised the subset/superset mismatch arm — half the ratchet's design rationale); `t4_failure_message_names_the_bound` (cited by the module doc but not previously written) now exists. A wrong CR cite (`106.12` for `ChooseColor`) is fixed to `614.12a`/`608.2d`. `look_at_top_or_route` and `wheel_hand`'s `why` text were both narrowed to state their true bound (upper-bound / CR 404.3 respectively) rather than overreach |

**Sequencing note.** PB-DP1..PB-DP6 need no wire change at all and could ship inside the
existing paused-queue cadence. PB-DP7..PB-DP9 are a coherent block that should be planned
together, because they all need the same missing machinery: a pending-decision that actually
*gates* progress. The engine already has that machinery seven times over
(`pending_commander_zone_choices`, `pending_zone_changes`, the three payment vectors,
`DredgeChoiceRequired`, `MiracleRevealChoiceRequired`) — but §4.4 and §4.11 show that only
`pending_zone_changes` genuinely blocks. **The generalisable design work is "make a pending
decision actually block", not "add another pending vector".**

> **UPDATED by PB-DP7 (`scutemob-155`).** The machinery now exists:
> `rules::engine::{BlockingDecision, blocking_decision}`, a progress guard in `enter_step` and
> an admission gate at the top of `process_command`. **PB-DP8 and PB-DP9 should read
> `memory/primitives/pb-plan-DP7.md` §1 before planning anything** — §1.5 says what DP-8
> inherits and what it must design fresh (its guard set is *not* this one; re-derive it from
> `flush_pending_triggers`'s call sites), and §1.6 says plainly that **DP-9 does not inherit
> the resume mechanism at all** — it pauses inside `execute_effect` and needs a resumable
> effect-list cursor (the OOS-DP5-5 problem), which is a separate `GameState` shape change.
>
> **CORRECTED by PB-DP9 (`scutemob-157`).** The first half of that sentence held — DP-9 does
> pause inside `execute_effect` and did need a `GameState` shape change. The second half did
> not: **"a resumable effect-list cursor ON THE STACK OBJECT" is impossible**, because
> `resolve_top_of_stack` pops the stack object (`resolution.rs:39-42`) before any effect runs.
> What shipped is an **abort-and-replay** — clone at entry, restore wholesale on suspension,
> bank the answer on `GameState` and re-run the resolution from the top — which needs no
> continuation structure at all and, unlike a cursor, makes "the suspended object leaves the
> stack" structurally unreachable instead of a live hazard. **OOS-DP5-5 is NOT closed by
> this**: a deferred draw suspends only its own effect, whereas PB-DP9 aborts the whole
> resolution, and the two mechanisms do not compose for free. See the PB-DP9 row above.
> PB-DP7 also established the block-vs-deadline test: **block only where the CR supplies no
> default.** PB-DP4's payments have CR 118.12a's "didn't pay" branch and live inside a
> priority window, so they stay deadlines; CR 514.1 has neither, so it blocks. Retrofitting
> the other six mechanisms onto the gate is **OOS-DP7-1**, and the dredge round-trip's
> "the engine pauses" doc comment turns out to be **fiction** (**OOS-DP7-2**).

wholesale by the next `/implement-primitive` run, so a seed recorded only there is lost —
seeds land **here**, in the suite's own binding spec. Same role §1c plays for the RS queue in
`memory/primitives/rider-seed-triage-2026-07-19.md`.

So (a) is **what fixing (c) alone would have created**: a permanent `ZoneId::Stack` leak in place of a silent no-op. A "just fix the lookup" change would have been strictly worse than HEAD, and this row's own "fix all three in one edit" was righter than its reasoning. (2) **(b) is unreachable by three mechanisms, not the one §1c of the v3 memo gives** — the ordering argument, *plus* `resolve_effect_target_list_indexed` dropping a dead `DeclaredTarget` (so the window is empty rather than narrow, even under CR 608.2b re-validation), *plus* nothing aiming a counter at a copy at all: a copy's stack-entry id is not a `state.objects` key, so `TargetSpell` validation refuses it **always**. (3) **(c) is the live shape and it is worse than "a silent no-op" sounds** — `TargetSpell` validation *accepts* the mutate spell's card, so the engine offers the target, takes the mana, and does nothing. (4) **The exposure was measured, not estimated: 66 live-wrong pairs** (6 `Complete` mutate defs × 11 counter defs), where the queue row implied 144 and this batch's own first SR-36 enumeration published **48** — that enumeration walked `Effect::CounterSpell` alone and was blind to `Effect::CounterUnlessPays`, which delegates into the same arm (`mana_leak`, `mana_tithe`, `make_disappear`, all `Complete`). **The check that caught all this was the check working**, as this row said — but note the corollary it did not: shape (c), the one that was actually live, produces **no divergence at all**, so `stack_consistency` could never have found it. | **OOS-DX25c-1** | **The retarget's per-index search is GREEDY, not combinatorially complete, so for a multi-target victim it can fail to find a legal reassignment that exists — via TWO distinct mechanisms, not one.** `rules::retarget::plan_target_change` walks each index in isolation, taking the first candidate whose TRIAL set validates rather than backtracking. (a) **No backtracking**: the shape Bolt Bend's 2024-11-08 ruling names directly ("you must change the target if possible") — a legal FINAL assignment can exist that the greedy walk never reaches because it committed to an earlier candidate. (b) **A trial is a MIXED set, not the final set** — index `i` holds the candidate under test, but every index `> i` still holds its ORIGINAL (undecided) target, which may already be illegal. `validate_targets_inner`'s two-pass best-fit assignment requires the WHOLE slice to be assignable, so ONE already-illegal original at an undecided index poisons EVERY candidate tried at an earlier index and the `?` at step 6 aborts the entire plan — even when a fully-legal final assignment exists. This directly contradicts CR 115.7a ("even if the original target is itself illegal by then") and CR 115.7e ("only the final set of targets is evaluated") for exactly the sets this mechanism evaluates: a genuinely CR 115.7e-compliant implementation would validate ONLY the actual final set (step 7 does this correctly, as the sole re-validation) and never let an intermediate/mixed trial's rejection abort the plan. (a) and (b) are independent failure mechanisms with the same symptom and the same safe failure direction. **Measured, not assumed, as zero-reachable today**: every `must_change: true` corpus member (`Bolt Bend`, `Misdirection`, `Untimely Malfunction`) requires the victim to declare EXACTLY ONE target (`R1` of `pb_dx25c_retarget_roster.rs` confirms both the roster and, per-member, that each one's own requirement is single-target-shaped), so `next.len()` is always 1, no trial ever contains an undecided original, and there is nothing for either mechanism to misfire on. ## 9. M11-local decision-loop extensibility assessment

Against `/home/skydude/projects/scutemob/.worktrees/scutemob-147/memory/m11-session-plan.md`
(read-only cross-worktree reference; nothing under `.worktrees/` was modified).

### 9.1 The question

The plan's §2(a) adopts a steppable driver:

```
    pub enum AdvanceOutcome { AwaitingHuman(PendingDecision), GameOver(..), Halted(..) }
    pub enum DecisionKind { Priority, Mulligan, CommanderZoneChoice,
                            DeclareAttackers, DeclareBlockers }
    pub struct HumanChoice { pub action_index: usize, pub params: ActionParams }
```

Does that generalise to trigger-time and resolution-time choices without redesign?

### 9.2 Answer: **no — and the plan's own reasoning shows why**

§2(a) justifies the design like this:

> **Sub-decisions**: the five non-`choose_action` `Bot` methods are *not* driver callbacks
> (verified: zero call sites), so there is nothing to intercept. Attackers, blockers,
> mulligan-bottoms and targets are all fields of the `Command` the seat returns. They become
> fields of `ActionParams` (§3), which is a server-side type — **no new `Command` or
> `GameEvent` variant.**

That is **exactly right for the five decisions it enumerates, and exactly wrong as a general
claim** — because it is true only of choices that are announced *at command-submission time*.
This audit's §4.6 through §4.11 are all choices that happen *inside* `process_command`, while
the engine flushes triggers or resolves a stack object. Concretely:

- `LocalGame::advance()` can only yield `AwaitingHuman` **between** `process_command` calls.
- `execute_effect_inner` returns `()` and cannot suspend (§4.9). **Still true after PB-DP9 —
  and that is why PB-DP9's mechanism is an ABORT, not a pause: the resolution is rolled back
  wholesale and re-run from the top once the answer arrives, so nothing has to suspend.**
- `flush_pending_triggers` runs to completion inside whatever command triggered it (§4.6/4.7).
- `ActionParams` is a *command-assembly* struct. There is no `Command` for a trigger target,
  a scry split, a search pick, or a cleanup discard, so there is nothing for `ActionParams` to
  assemble.

So `DecisionKind`'s five variants are not an early cut of a longer list — they are **the
complete set of decisions reachable by this architecture**, and they will stay complete until
the *engine* grows pending-decision state for the other classes. That is a wire change, which
the plan's §7 constraint 6 explicitly forbids:

> **OVERTAKEN BY EVENTS (PB-DP7/DP8/DP9, `scutemob-155`/`156`/`157`).** The engine grew exactly
> that pending-decision state, three times, outside M11-local and therefore outside constraint
> 6's scope. `DecisionKind` now has **seven** variants, three of which are out-of-band blocking
> decisions (`CleanupDiscard`, `TriggerTargets`, `EffectChoice`), and PROTOCOL went 27 → **31**
> in the process. The paragraph's *analysis* was right — it correctly predicted that reaching
> the trigger-time and resolution-time classes needs engine pending state and a wire change —
> and its *conclusion* ("they will stay complete") was a scoping assumption, not a structural
> one. Read the numbers below as of 2026-07-26, not as current.

> **No new `Command` / `GameEvent` / `Effect` variant.** If one seems necessary, stop and
> flag: it is a wire change (SR-8) requiring a PROTOCOL bump, and for this milestone it
> signals a design error.

**This is not a criticism of the plan.** Constraint 6 is right for M11-local, and the audit
confirms the plan's own §1 fact 6 (optional payments are "not stalls; just silently
unavailable"). The problem is only that a closed 5-variant `DecisionKind` and a flat
`actions: Vec<LegalAction>` will *look* complete to session 5 and 7 authors, and the DTO
shapes they lock in will have to be reshaped later. The fix is cheap and belongs in the
sessions that define those shapes.

### 9.3 The engine already has the right pattern — it just doesn't block

Seven existing round-trips prove the shape generalises at the engine level:
`ReplacementChoiceRequired`/`OrderReplacements`, `CommanderZoneReturnChoiceRequired`,
`DredgeChoiceRequired`/`ChooseDredge`, `MiracleRevealChoiceRequired`/`ChooseMiracle`,
`EchoPaymentRequired`/`PayEcho`, `CumulativeUpkeepPaymentRequired`, `RecoverPaymentRequired`.
Each is: emit a `*Required` event → record a pending entry → accept an answering `Command`.

But §4.4 and §4.11 show that **only `pending_zone_changes` actually gates anything**. The
other five pending vectors are inert queues that nothing consults. So the reusable asset is
the *event + command + pending-entry triple*; the missing piece is the gate. That is why
PB-DP7 in §8 is proposed as a deliberate pilot.

> **UPDATED by PB-DP7 (`scutemob-155`).** The gate now exists —
> `rules::engine::{BlockingDecision, blocking_decision}`, consulted in `enter_step` (progress)
> and at the top of `process_command` (admission), with a clear-on-concede in `handle_concede`.
> **None of the seven existing round-trips was retrofitted onto it** (OOS-DP7-1), and the
> paragraph above needs one correction: the dredge round-trip does not merely fail to block —
> its own doc comments *claim* it does. `events.rs:848-850` and `replacement.rs:619` both say
> "the engine pauses"; `perform_one_draw` records no pending state and `DrawStepOutcome`'s doc
> at `:764-767` says the caller does not stop. See **OOS-DP7-2**.
>
> **UPDATED again by PB-DX2 (`scutemob-162`, R9 re-review correction).** "Only
> `pending_zone_changes` actually gates anything" is now stale on a second axis:
> `pending_draws` gates `Command::ChooseDredge` (`replacement::handle_choose_dredge` requires and
> consumes an outstanding entry — before PB-DX2 the command validated only the card, never that a
> draw was pending). This is a *command-level* gate (rejects an ill-timed `ChooseDredge`), not a
> *progress* gate in `BlockingDecision`'s sense (nothing blocks priority/step advancement waiting
> for an answer — see **OOS-DP5-2**), so it does not move the block-vs-deadline classification
> above, but the blanket "inert queues that nothing consults" claim about the other five pending
> vectors was already inaccurate by the time this note was written and is corrected here rather
> than left for a third reader to catch.

### 9.4 Concrete recommendations

**Session 3** — *Action parameterization + engine target queries*

1. Make `DecisionKind` `#[non_exhaustive]` and document, in the enum's doc comment, that it
   enumerates **command-submission-time** decisions only, with a pointer to this audit for the
   trigger-time and resolution-time classes it structurally cannot reach. One comment now
   prevents a later reader assuming the surface is complete.
   **DONE by PB-DP7 (`scutemob-155`)** — the attribute is on, and `DecisionKind::CleanupDiscard`
   is the first variant that is *not* a priority window, which is the concrete proof the
   recommendation was needed. Note the premise has moved: the enum is no longer
   command-submission-time-only.
   **AND THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS NOW FALSIFIED (PB-DP9, `scutemob-157`).** This item said the
   enum "structurally cannot reach" the trigger-time and resolution-time classes. PB-DP8 added
   `DecisionKind::TriggerTargets` and PB-DP9 added `DecisionKind::EffectChoice`, so it reaches
   both — and reaching the resolution-time class needed no reshaping of `PendingDecision`
   either, because the abort-and-replay design hands the client an ordinary
   `Vec<LegalAction>` on a state that has been rolled back to look exactly like a state where
   nothing has started. Item 2 below is therefore still un-done and still un-needed.
2. Give `PendingDecision` an explicit shape for its payload rather than only
   `actions: Vec<LegalAction>` — e.g. `payload: DecisionPayload` with an `Actions(Vec<LegalAction>)`
   variant today. A future `TriggerOrder`/`ResolutionChoice` then adds a variant instead of
   reshaping the struct that sessions 5 and 7 will have built DTOs against.
3. **Surface the decisions that are already reachable with zero wire change.** The plan's §1
   fact 6 lists them; this audit adds why they matter. `advance()` should yield `AwaitingHuman`
   for a non-empty `pending_echo_payments` / `pending_cumulative_upkeep_payments` /
   `pending_recover_payments`, and `OrderBlockers` should be offered whenever an attacker has
   ≥2 blockers. These need new `LegalAction` variants (simulator-internal, **not** a wire
   change) and are the cheapest agency the milestone can buy. Note **DP-11**: because nothing
   enforces the pending payments, an M11 game today lets every echo permanent stay for free.

   > **UPDATED by PB-DP4 (`scutemob-152`).** The `LegalAction` half is **DONE** for all three
   > payments; the enforcement gap is closed; and **the `advance()` half turned out to be
   > unnecessary**. Because the deadline makes the payment a choice inside a normal priority
   > window rather than an out-of-band pause, `LegalAction::PayEcho` / `PayCumulativeUpkeep` /
   > `PayRecover` arrive inside the **existing** `PendingDecision` and are classified
   > `DecisionKind::Priority` by `decision_kind_for` — **no new `DecisionKind` variant, no
   > `PendingDecision` reshaping, no `local_game.rs` edit at all.** Cheaper than this
   > recommendation predicted. The `OrderBlockers` half (**DP-13**) remains open and is still
   > the only decision in this list with no `LegalAction`.
4. ~~Session 3 item 5 already forbids re-deriving `hybrid_choices` / `phyrexian_life_payments`.
   Extend the same rule to `modes_chosen`: **`action_to_command_with_params` must reject an
   empty `modes_chosen` on a modal action whose `min_modes >= 1`**, because the engine will not
   (**DP-4**). Otherwise the first human to cast Cryptic Command through the play server gets
   half a spell at full price and no error.~~
   **SUPERSEDED by PB-DP3 (`scutemob-151`)** — the engine now rejects it, at cast time and
   before costs are paid, so the play server needs no compensating check. What it needs instead
   is a mode-selection **UI**: `crates/simulator/src/legal_actions.rs`'s `spell_default_modes` /
   `ability_default_modes` supply the first `min_modes` legal indices as a bot/placeholder
   default, and that placeholder is exactly what session 7 must replace with a human choice.
   Note also **OOS-DP3-7**: the ~28 alt-cost cast paths cannot announce modes at all, so a
   modal card cast via flashback/escape/etc. is unreachable through them today.

**Session 5** — *play-server REST API*

5. Make `DecisionView` a **tagged union keyed on decision kind**, not a flat
   `{seq, kind, actions}`. `POST /api/game/action` should carry the same discriminator. A
   trigger-ordering decision is a permutation, a scry decision is a partition, a cleanup
   discard is a subset — none of them is an index into an action list, and a client written
   against a flat action list will need a breaking change to accept any of them.
   **SHARPENED by PB-DP7 (`scutemob-155`), and now urgent.** The cleanup discard shipped, and
   the subset shape this recommendation predicted is exactly what `Command::DiscardToHandSize
   { player, cards: Vec<ObjectId> }` carries. It fits the flat `actions: Vec<LegalAction>` only
   because the whole subset is packed inside one `LegalAction` — i.e. it is **the last decision
   class that fits at all**. Make the reshape (rec 2's `payload: DecisionPayload`) *before*
   PB-DP8 rather than after; seeded as **OOS-DP7-5**.
   **"The last decision class that fits at all" is now falsified twice over.** PB-DP8's
   per-slot target announcement and PB-DP9's scry/surveil **partition** -- precisely the shape
   this recommendation named as not fitting -- both packed into one `LegalAction` the same way:
   `AnswerEffectChoice { choice_id, source, question, answer }` carries the full legal answer
   space in `question` and an engine-accepted default in `answer`. The reshape is still worth
   doing for the *client*'s sake (a picker needs the discriminator), but the flat action list
   has not yet been the thing that blocks a decision class from shipping. OOS-DP7-5 stands,
   with its urgency downgraded.
6. On the R4 `--dev` raw-command escape hatch the plan defers to this session: **recommend
   yes**, and note that it is also the only way a playtester can currently exercise
   `PayEcho`, `PayCumulativeUpkeep`, `PayRecover` and `OrderBlockers` (no `LegalAction`
   exists for any of them, §4.11 / DP-11 / DP-13).
   **SUPERSEDED IN PART by PB-DP4 (`scutemob-152`)** — `LegalAction::PayEcho`,
   `PayCumulativeUpkeep` and `PayRecover` now exist and reach a human seat through the normal
   priority decision, so the raw-command hatch is no longer the only way to exercise them. The
   `--dev` hatch is still recommended, and **`OrderBlockers` is now the only decision in the
   audit with no `LegalAction`**.
7. `GET /api/game/report` (session 8 item 5) should include the auto-choice annotations from
   recommendation 8 below, so a "that seemed wrong" report distinguishes an engine bug from an
   engine *choice*.

**Session 7** — *Targeting, combat and choice UIs*

8. **Ship an "engine chose this for you" annotation in the event feed.** This is the single
   highest-value item the milestone can add for this audit's findings, it needs no wire change,
   and it converts an invisible wrongness into a visible one. Minimum viable set, all
   detectable from existing `GameEvent`s plus the seat view: triggered-ability targets
   (**DP-6**), scry/surveil disposition (**DP-8/DP-9**), search picks (**DP-7**), sacrifice and
   discard picks (**DP-16**, ~~**DP-3**~~ — DP-3 no longer needs an annotation, PB-DP7 made it a
   real choice; but see **OOS-DP7-6**, the TUI answers it with the old auto-pick), and combat
   damage assignment (**DP-13**).
9. `TargetPicker.svelte` is the **cast-time** picker (CR 601.2c). Name it accordingly and
   document that trigger targets (CR 603.3d) never reach it. Otherwise session 7 will close
   believing targeting is done.
10. The attacker picker should not imply the engine will enforce attack requirements
    maximally — §4.5 shows validation is per-declaration only, so a client that offers an
    under-satisfying attack set gets a rejection, not a correction. And per **DP-10**, if a
    Propaganda-class effect is out, the UI must not tell the human they paid: nothing is
    debited.
11. Session 7's acceptance is "the human can attack, block, and cast targeted/X/modal spells".
    Add: **and can see, in the feed, every choice the engine made on their behalf.**

### 9.5 What does *not* need to change

The plan's crate layout, its async boundary, `Viewer`-based redaction, the steppable-driver
decision over the channel-backed bot, and constraint 6 are all sound and this audit does not
touch them. `LocalGame` is the right home for a decision loop; it just needs to be honest
about which decisions it can currently reach.
