## 10. Re-audit triggers

> **PB-DP10 mechanization ledger (`scutemob-158`).** Of the eight triggers below, **2 are now
> MECHANIZED** (a test computes and enforces the answer on every `cargo test`), **2 are
> feasible-but-not-built and now carry a seed** (the DSL-enum roster digest, **OOS-DP10-11**;
> the `GameEvent` roster digest, **OOS-DP10-7**), and **4 stay human** (DP-24's
> accepted-and-discarded-`Command`-field check, **OOS-DP10-4**; a new `BlockingDecision`
> variant's seven obligations; a new same-zone `move_object_to_zone` caller, **OOS-DP9-11**;
> a `Zone` API change). Write that ratio down rather than a claim of coverage — this suite's
> recurring lesson (OOS-DP7-11; PB-DP8's meta-lesson iii) is that *a gate cited as covering
> something is a claim like any other*, and **the first version of this very ledger said
> "3 of 8" while its own body concluded the third one "stays NOT mechanized"** — caught by
> the closing `/review`. Counting your own coverage is the same kind of claim.
> **MECHANIZED**: the §3.1 re-derivation (below, `decision_site_reconciliation_report`); the
> `docs/authoring-status.md` material-jump trigger (the same test prints the live
> denominator and percentage every run, and `T6`'s exact ratchet catches the numerator).
> **A third, narrower one**: a gate over the CORPUS cannot see a new `Effect`/
> `AbilityDefinition`/`ReplacementModification` variant no def yet uses — but that variant
> ALREADY forces a PROTOCOL and a HASH bump (both are in the SR-8/SR-17 wire closures), so
> the *notice* was never the missing half; the missing half is the *obligation* to classify
> it in `ROWS` and update §3.1/§10, which nothing states today and which a roster digest
> (count + blake3 of the sorted variant-name list) could supply — **not built in PB-DP10**
> (budget; see **OOS-DP10-11**, filed by the closing review after the WIP's own record of
> this drop was found to point at the wrong seeds), so this one stays **NOT mechanized**
> below — **feasible and seeded, not mechanized**. The `GameEvent` sibling-answer sweep is the
> same instrument pointed at another enum and is in the same state (**OOS-DP10-7**).
> **STAYS HUMAN**: DP-24's accepted-and-discarded-`Command`-field check (**OOS-DP10-4**); any
> new `BlockingDecision` variant's seven obligations (only 2 of 7 are compile-forced, per
> PB-DP9's own count); any new same-zone `move_object_to_zone` caller (OOS-DP9-11 already owns
> that sweep, unbuilt); and a `Zone` API change, whose roster §10 already prescribes deriving
> from `Zone::push_front` call sites by hand.

Per [methodology.md](methodology.md) "When to Re-Audit":

- Any new `Effect` variant that carries a `choices`, `optional`, `may`, or filter-selection
  field — check whether it joins §3.1 or is gated.
  > **PARTIALLY MECHANIZED, AND THE FRAMING WAS THE WRONG ONE (PB-DP10, `scutemob-158`).** A
  > gate over card defs cannot see a variant no def uses — correct, and why a roster digest
  > has to scan the DSL *declaration*, not the corpus. But the honest marginal value is
  > smaller than the trigger implies: `Effect` is already in both the SR-8 and SR-17
  > closures, so a new variant already forces a PROTOCOL and a HASH bump — the **notice** is
  > free; what a digest would add is the **obligation** message ("classify it in `ROWS`"). A
  > needle scan for choice-shaped fields would also be worse than a whole-roster digest: the
  > DSL has only **four** such fields (`prompt`/`choices` on `Choose`, `optional` on
  > `LookAtTopThenPlace`, and the mode-target machinery), while `Proliferate`, `SearchLibrary`,
  > `Scry`, `DiscardCards`, `SacrificePermanents`, `Bolster`, `Connive`, `PutOnLibrary`,
  > `Discover`, `ChangeTargets` and `TheRingTemptsYou` carry **no** decision-shaped field at
  > all — the choice is inherent in the CR keyword action, not in the DSL shape. Not built
  > this batch (budget; owning seed **OOS-DP10-11**, filed by the closing review — the WIP's
  > own record of the drop pointed at two seeds that own a DIFFERENT enum's digest, not this
  > one); recommendation for whoever builds it: ship a whole-roster digest, not a needle scan,
  > and do not let the trigger's wording imply the needle set is the population.
- Any new `Command` variant — check whether it closes a §5 finding or is another
  accepted-and-discarded field (**DP-24**).
  > **NOT mechanized (PB-DP10, `scutemob-158`).** Feasible test-only as an SR-15-style scan
  > for `_`-bound `Command` fields in handlers; unbuilt. See **OOS-DP10-4**.
- After **PB-DP7** or any first pending-decision-that-blocks lands — re-run §3.1's sweep and
  re-derive the 277 figure. Exclude `defs/mod.rs`, and remember the union must include the
  modal-triggered-ability row — omitting it is how the first pass of this audit undercounted by 5.
  > **FIRED 2026-07-26** — PB-DP7 (`scutemob-155`) landed the first blocking pending decision,
  > and `Command::DiscardToHandSize` is the new `Command` the trigger above also names (that
  > one is already answered: **not** an accepted-and-discarded field, every field is validated).
  > **The §3.1 re-derivation is still owed** — tracked as **OOS-DP7-7**. A third trigger also
  > fired that this list did not have: a new `GameEvent` needs a `reveals_hidden_info` decision,
  > and checking it turned up a pre-existing wrong answer on a sibling (**OOS-DP7-3**). Add

  > **MECHANIZED — CLOSES OOS-DP7-7 (PB-DP10, `scutemob-158`).** The 277-def re-derivation is

- Any new `GameEvent` variant — decide its `reveals_hidden_info()` answer deliberately and
